signals.title: Missile fired at container ship transiting Bab el-Mandeb; crew unharmed
signals.summary: A 9,400 TEU container vessel reported a near-miss missile strike 18 nm west of Mokha while transiting the Bab el-Mandeb strait northbound. UKMTO confirmed the incident and raised its regional alert level.
signals.plainEnglish: A commercial ship was shot at in the narrow entrance to the Red Sea. Warships are responding, and insurers will treat this stretch of water as significantly more dangerous starting immediately.
signals.notImplied: This does NOT imply the strait is closed, that any OceanMind vessel was targeted, or that Suez transits are suspended — traffic continues at elevated risk.

signals.title: UKMTO raises Red Sea threat level to SEVERE after second drone incident
signals.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations elevated its threat assessment for the southern Red Sea to SEVERE following a one-way drone attack on a products tanker 40 nm north of the Hanish Islands.
signals.plainEnglish: The official maritime security watchdog for the region now rates attacks as likely rather than possible. Ships are being told to consider alternative routing.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply naval escorts are unavailable or that all cargo classes face equal risk — car carriers and container tonnage have been preferentially targeted.

signals.title: War-risk premiums for Red Sea transits quadruple to 0.9% of hull value
signals.summary: Lloyd's market underwriters raised additional war-risk premiums for Red Sea / Gulf of Aden transits from 0.22% to 0.9% of hull value, with several syndicates declining container tonnage outright.
signals.plainEnglish: Insuring a single Suez voyage for a large container ship now costs roughly USD 400,000 more than last week — if cover can be found at all.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply cover is formally withdrawn; it remains available at sharply higher cost and with 48-hour notice-of-transit clauses.

signals.title: Two container lines announce immediate Cape of Good Hope diversions
signals.summary: Two of the five largest container carriers instructed all Asia–Europe strings to divert via the Cape of Good Hope until further notice, citing crew safety and insurance economics.
signals.plainEnglish: Major competitors are already rerouting around Africa. Expect southbound Indian Ocean traffic to rise and Suez slot availability to fall.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply an industry-wide mandate — several carriers continue Suez transits with armed escorts and convoy timing.

signals.title: Coalition navies begin escorted convoy scheme through Bab el-Mandeb
signals.summary: A multinational naval task force announced twice-weekly escorted convoys through the Bab el-Mandeb corridor, with slots allocated 72 hours in advance and capped at 12 vessels per convoy.
signals.plainEnglish: Protected passage exists but is scarce: two convoys a week, twelve ships each, booked three days ahead. Missing a slot means anchoring in a threat area.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply convoy passage removes risk — escorted vessels have still been approached, and waiting at the convoy anchorage carries its own exposure.

signals.title: Suez Canal daily transits fall 38% week-on-week as carriers divert
signals.summary: Suez Canal Authority movement data shows southbound + northbound transits dropped from 62 to 39 per day. SCA offered a 15% toll rebate for July bookings to retain traffic.
signals.plainEnglish: Traffic through Suez is collapsing as ships avoid the Red Sea approach. The canal is discounting tolls, but the bottleneck is the strait south of it, not the canal itself.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply the canal is obstructed or that transit times inside the canal have changed.

signals.title: UNCTAD: Red Sea disruption could add 0.4pp to global consumer inflation
signals.summary: UNCTAD's rapid assessment estimates prolonged Red Sea diversions raise Asia–Europe container costs 42% and could add up to 0.4 percentage points to global consumer price inflation over 12 months.
signals.plainEnglish: This is a macro-scale disruption: rerouting is expensive enough, for long enough, to show up in worldwide consumer prices.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply container capacity is physically insufficient — longer routes absorb tonnage but the fleet can still carry demand.

signals.title: Galaxy-class car carrier reports small-arms fire near Hanish Islands
signals.summary: A PCTC en route Jeddah–Singapore reported small-arms fire from two skiffs 25 nm southeast of the Hanish Islands; the vessel executed evasive manoeuvres and continued.
signals.plainEnglish: Attacks are not limited to drones and missiles — small fast boats are also harassing ships along the same corridor.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply a boarding was attempted or that the skiffs pursued beyond the immediate area.

signals.title: Egypt convenes emergency shipping summit over canal revenue collapse
signals.summary: Egypt's government convened carriers and P&I clubs in Cairo to discuss transit guarantees, after canal revenues fell an estimated USD 180M month-on-month.
signals.plainEnglish: Diplomatic efforts to restore Suez traffic are starting, but no security guarantee exists yet that insurers accept.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply a resolution timeline — previous escalation cycles took 6–14 weeks to normalise.

signals.title: Singapore bunker demand spikes 22% as diverted tonnage tops up for Cape runs
signals.summary: MPA weekly figures show bunker sales up 22% w/w as Asia–Europe services take maximum fuel before the longer Cape routing. VLSFO barge slots quoted at 3–4 days' wait.
signals.plainEnglish: Ships preparing to sail around Africa are filling their tanks in Singapore, straining barge availability and pushing local fuel prices up.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply Singapore is out of fuel — the constraint is barge scheduling, not inventory.

signals.title: Port Klang Westports reports berth waiting up to 30 hours
signals.summary: Westports Malaysia reported container berth waiting times of 24–30 hours as diverted services re-sequence port rotations, versus a 6-hour norm.
signals.plainEnglish: Port Klang is congested because rerouting ships changed their port call order all at once. Waiting a day-plus for a berth is now normal there.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply cargo operations are slower once berthed — crane productivity is unchanged.

signals.title: Malacca Strait VTS logs record daily transits as reroutes concentrate traffic
signals.summary: Klang VTS recorded 312 transits in 24 hours, the highest this year, as Cape-bound and Suez-bound traffic overlap in the strait.
signals.plainEnglish: The Malacca Strait is busier than ever — more ships in the same narrow water means more collision-avoidance manoeuvring and slower effective transits.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply any incident occurred or that transit is restricted.

signals.title: Colombo transshipment yard utilisation hits 92%
signals.summary: Colombo's main terminal reported 92% yard utilisation as Indian Ocean transshipment cargo builds ahead of longer Cape rotations.
signals.plainEnglish: A key relay port on the Asia–Europe route is nearly full, which slows container connections for cargo changing ships there.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply vessel berthing delays yet — the pressure is in the container yard, not at the quay.

signals.title: Typhoon Mirinae intensifies to Category 3 east of Luzon
signals.summary: JTWC upgraded Typhoon Mirinae to Category 3 with 100 kt sustained winds, tracking WNW at 12 kt toward the Luzon Strait; landfall or recurvature expected within 72 hours.
signals.plainEnglish: A major typhoon sits across the main Taiwan–Philippines shipping corridor. Transpacific services must decide now whether to route north or south of it.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply Taiwanese or Philippine ports are closed yet — closures typically begin 24–36 h before landfall.

signals.title: Southwest monsoon surge brings 5m swells to Arabian Sea lanes
signals.summary: IMD reported a strong monsoon surge generating 4.5–5.5 m significant wave heights across the Arabian Sea west of 70°E, expected to persist 5–7 days.
signals.plainEnglish: Heavy seas between India and the Gulf of Aden will slow ships and increase fuel burn on that leg for about a week.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply routes must change — this is a seasonal slowdown, not a hazard requiring diversion.

signals.title: Agulhas Current advisory: abnormal wave risk off Wild Coast
signals.summary: South African Weather Service issued its standing winter advisory for abnormal waves (>10 m possible) where southwesterly gales oppose the Agulhas Current between Durban and East London.
signals.plainEnglish: Ships rounding South Africa in winter must respect the classic freak-wave zone off the Wild Coast — routing slightly offshore and slowing in gales is standard practice.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply the Cape route is unsafe — thousands of transits handle this with routine seamanship; it is a planning input, not a blocker.

signals.title: Panama Canal raises daily transit slots to 34 as Gatún Lake recovers
signals.summary: The Panama Canal Authority increased booking slots from 31 to 34/day, citing improved Gatún Lake levels after early wet-season rainfall; draft limit unchanged at 49 ft.
signals.plainEnglish: Panama is recovering from last year's drought restrictions — slightly more ships can transit daily, easing the backlog on Asia–US East Coast routes.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply pre-drought capacity (36–38/day) is restored, nor that draft limits have been lifted.

signals.title: North Sea summer gale warning: 45 kt gusts in Dover Strait approaches
signals.summary: UK Met Office issued a gale warning for Dover Strait and southern North Sea, with 40–45 kt gusts and 3.5 m seas for 36 hours from 15 July.
signals.plainEnglish: Short, sharp summer storm at the English Channel entrance — arrival timing into Rotterdam may slip a few hours; pilot boarding could pause at the peak.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply Rotterdam port closure — the port operates through gales; only pilotage windows tighten.

signals.title: La Niña watch: BoM flags elevated cyclone risk for 2026-27 Australian season
signals.summary: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology moved to La Niña WATCH, historically correlated with an earlier and more active Coral Sea cyclone season.
signals.plainEnglish: A seasonal heads-up: iron-ore and coal routes off Australia may see more weather interruptions from November onward.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply any near-term operational impact — this is a 4-month-out planning signal.

signals.title: EU ETS maritime: 2026 surrender obligation confirmed at 70% incl. CH₄ and N₂O
signals.summary: The European Commission confirmed the 2026 maritime EU ETS phase-in: operators surrender allowances for 70% of verified 2025 emissions, with methane and nitrous oxide newly in scope from 1 January 2026.
signals.plainEnglish: Carbon costs for voyages touching the EU step up this year — 70% of emissions must be paid for (100% from 2027), and two extra greenhouse gases now count.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply non-EU voyages are charged — only 50% of emissions on voyages into/out of the EU, 100% within the EU, are in scope.

signals.title: FuelEU Maritime: first compliance balances due; pooling market opens
signals.summary: Verifiers began issuing 2025 FuelEU GHG-intensity balances (limit 89.34 gCO₂e/MJ). A compliance-pooling marketplace opened with surplus prices around €320/tCO₂e.
signals.plainEnglish: Ships trading to Europe now have a fuel carbon-intensity score with real money attached — clean-fuel surpluses can be sold, deficits must be bought or penalised.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply conventional VLSFO becomes non-compliant — blending small bio fractions typically maintains compliance through 2029.

signals.title: IMO MEPC 84 advances Net-Zero Framework: global GHG levy vote set for October
signals.summary: MEPC 84 concluded with draft text for a global GHG fuel intensity standard and a levy mechanism, scheduled for adoption vote at an extraordinary session in October 2026.
signals.plainEnglish: A worldwide carbon price for shipping moved one step closer — pricing decisions made now should assume a global levy from 2028.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply the levy is agreed — the October vote could still fail or dilute the measure.

signals.title: MPA Singapore mandates digital bunkering documentation from 1 October
signals.summary: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore confirmed e-BDN (electronic bunker delivery notes) become mandatory for all licensed suppliers from 1 October 2026, ending paper BDNs.
signals.plainEnglish: Bunkering paperwork in Singapore goes fully digital this autumn — quantity disputes get easier to audit and mass-flow-meter data becomes the single source of truth.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply other ports follow the same timeline; Rotterdam and Fujairah have not announced mandates.

signals.title: AMSA detains two bulkers in Newcastle over CII record irregularities
signals.summary: The Australian Maritime Safety Authority detained two Capesize bulkers after port state control found fuel-consumption records inconsistent with reported CII data.
signals.plainEnglish: Regulators are now actively auditing carbon-intensity paperwork at the berth — falsified or sloppy fuel records get ships detained.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply industry-wide fraud — two detentions from ~400 inspections this quarter.

signals.title: EU adds three shadow-fleet tankers to sanctions list after dark STS off Malaysia
signals.summary: The EU's 19th sanctions package designated three aframax tankers observed conducting dark ship-to-ship transfers in the South China Sea off eastern Malaysia.
signals.plainEnglish: Chartering or bunkering near sanctioned shadow-fleet vessels creates compliance exposure — counterparty screening matters more in Southeast Asian anchorages.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply Malaysian ports or legitimate STS operations are sanctioned.

signals.title: IMB: armed robbery attempts in Singapore Strait up 40% year-on-year
signals.summary: The ICC International Maritime Bureau logged 47 boarding attempts in the Singapore Strait January–June 2026, mostly opportunistic theft from bulkers underway at night in the eastbound lane.
signals.plainEnglish: Petty sea-robbery in the Singapore Strait keeps rising — extra lookouts and locked deck stores are standard mitigation; cargo and crew risk remains low.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply hijack risk — no vessel control incidents recorded; these are theft events.

signals.title: Gulf of Guinea: crew kidnapping from product tanker 90 nm off Brass
signals.summary: Five crew were taken from a product tanker in a night boarding 90 nm south of Brass, Nigeria — the third kidnap-for-ransom incident in the Gulf of Guinea this quarter.
signals.plainEnglish: West African piracy remains the world's most dangerous for crews. Ships transiting the Gulf of Guinea need hardened routines and ideally escort in the highest-risk box.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply the Cape route to Europe is affected — incidents concentrate within 150 nm of the Niger Delta, far east of the Cape–Europe track.

signals.title: Somali basin: first skiff approach reported in 14 months
signals.summary: A bulk carrier reported a two-skiff approach 280 nm east of Mogadishu; the vessel increased speed and the skiffs broke off. First such report since May 2025.
signals.plainEnglish: A reminder that Somali piracy is dormant, not extinct — ships shifting to Cape routings should still follow BMP5 hardening through the western Indian Ocean.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply a resurgence — a single approach with no weapons sighted.

signals.title: Hormuz: IRGC seizes tanker in dispute over cargo documentation
signals.summary: Iranian forces boarded and detained a Marshall Islands-flag products tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, citing a commercial cargo dispute. Transit traffic otherwise normal.
signals.plainEnglish: One-off tanker detention in Hormuz — the strait remains open, but Gulf loadings carry familiar low-probability, high-impact seizure risk.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply a blockade or broader interference pattern; 110+ vessels transited normally the same day.

signals.title: South China Sea: coast guard standoff near Second Thomas Shoal resupply
signals.summary: Philippine and Chinese coast guard vessels shadowed each other during a resupply mission; water cannon used, no collision. Commercial routing unaffected.
signals.plainEnglish: Tensions flare periodically along the main South China Sea lane, but commercial traffic continues on normal routes with no interference.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply any restriction on merchant shipping lanes through the area.

signals.title: Taiwan Strait transit advisory renewed ahead of August exercises window
signals.summary: Regional navies renewed advisories for the Taiwan Strait ahead of an announced PLA exercise window in early August; carriers weighing east-of-Taiwan routings.
signals.plainEnglish: Nothing has changed yet, but early August could bring temporary exercise closures east of the strait — schedules touching Taiwan should hold buffer.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply current transits are restricted.

signals.title: Rotterdam box terminals warn of peak-season yard density from Cape arrivals bunching
signals.summary: Port of Rotterdam Authority flagged that Cape-diverted services arriving off-window are bunching arrivals, lifting yard density to 85% at the largest deep-sea terminals.
signals.plainEnglish: Rotterdam is absorbing irregular arrivals caused by reroutes — expect a day or two of extra berth waiting into August.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply congestion at Maasvlakte anchorages today — waiting is currently under 24 hours.

signals.title: Durban bunker availability tightens; VLSFO premium +US$28/t over Singapore
signals.summary: Cape-routed traffic lifted Durban bunker demand sharply; suppliers quote 4–6 day lead times and a US$28/t premium to Singapore VLSFO.
signals.plainEnglish: Fuelling in South Africa is getting expensive and slow as everyone reroutes — better to load maximum fuel in Asia before the Cape leg.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply Durban cannot supply — lead times are manageable with 5+ days notice.

signals.title: VLSFO Singapore hits US$612/t, up 5.5% on reroute demand
signals.summary: Singapore VLSFO assessments rose to US$612/t as Cape diversions add ~15% distance to Asia–Europe voyages and demand pulls forward.
signals.plainEnglish: Fuel itself is getting pricier because everyone suddenly needs more of it — longer routes burn more, and buyers are topping up early.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply a supply shortage — refinery output is normal; this is a demand-driven move.

signals.title: Shanghai container spot rates to N. Europe jump 31% in one week
signals.summary: SCFI Europe leg printed a 31% w/w increase as carriers apply emergency surcharges and blank sailings to cover Cape diversions.
signals.plainEnglish: Freight rates are surging — the cost of the disruption is being passed to shippers within days, not months.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply capacity is unavailable — bookings remain open at the higher rates.

signals.title: Ningbo-Zhoushan resumes full operations after 12-hour fog closure
signals.summary: Dense fog closed Ningbo-Zhoushan approaches for 12 hours; pilotage resumed with a 15-vessel inbound queue cleared within a day.
signals.plainEnglish: Brief weather pause at the world's busiest cargo port — schedules recovered within a day; minimal ripple effects.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply lasting congestion.

signals.title: Jebel Ali launches green methanol bunkering pilot with two supply barges
signals.summary: DP World and ENOC began a green methanol bunkering pilot at Jebel Ali, initially serving two methanol-dual-fuel container vessels monthly.
signals.plainEnglish: Another major hub can now fuel methanol-powered ships — the alternative-fuel network keeps expanding along the Asia–Europe corridor.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply commercial-scale availability — volumes are pilot-level for now.

signals.title: Chittagong anchorage waiting doubles amid monsoon lighterage delays
signals.summary: Monsoon swells halved lighterage productivity at Chittagong outer anchorage; bulker waiting times doubled to 8–10 days.
signals.plainEnglish: Bangladesh's main port is badly slowed by seasonal weather — bulk cargoes routed there face over a week of waiting.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply container berths are equally affected — the delay is concentrated in outer-anchorage bulk lighterage.

signals.title: Ambrey: targeting pattern analysis shows container tonnage at highest risk band
signals.summary: Security consultancy Ambrey's pattern analysis of 31 Red Sea incidents since May shows large container vessels and car carriers drawing 71% of attacks despite being 38% of transits.
signals.plainEnglish: If you operate big container ships, your class of vessel is the preferred target in the Red Sea right now — the risk is not evenly shared.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply tankers and bulkers are safe — they account for the remaining 29% of incidents.

signals.title: Kra Isthmus land-bridge feasibility study revived by Thai government
signals.summary: Thailand's cabinet approved budget for a refreshed feasibility study of the Kra land-bridge as Malacca congestion and Red Sea instability renew interest in alternatives.
signals.plainEnglish: Long-shot infrastructure news: a Thai land route bypassing Malacca is being studied again. Nothing changes operationally for years, if ever.
signals.notImplied: Does NOT imply construction is approved or financed.

routeOptions.label: Option A — Suez Canal (plan of record)
routeOptions.notes: War-risk premium now ≈ USD 400k for this transit; underwriters require 48 h notice and convoy slot (2/week, 12 vessels). Container tonnage is the preferred attack target class.

routeOptions.label: Option B — Cape of Good Hope + slow-steam ×2 (recommended)
routeOptions.notes: Slow-steam Wild Coast + Dakar segments (19.5 → 16.0 kn) cuts the CO₂ penalty from +11.8% to +5.9% via the speed-cube rule. Avoids war-risk premium entirely.

routeOptions.label: Option C — Cape of Good Hope, full speed
routeOptions.notes: 2 days faster than Option B but burns +168 t more fuel and emits +530 tCO₂ more; fails the carbon-aware ranking and worsens the FuelEU trajectory.

routeOptions.label: Great circle — North Pacific (slow-steam for FuelEU pool credit)
Direct — Makassar Strait / South China Sea
Direct — Hormuz / Malacca
routeOptions.notes: Monsoon swell adds ~0.5 kn speed loss across the Arabian Sea leg this week.

routeOptions.label: Great circle — north of Typhoon Mirinae (original)
routeOptions.notes: Crosses Typhoon Mirinae forecast cone within 48 h — heavy-weather exposure.

routeOptions.label: Southern deviation — clear of typhoon cone (active)
routeOptions.notes: Adds 310 nm but keeps 240+ nm separation from the typhoon track.

routeOptions.label: Transpacific — Panama Canal
routeOptions.notes: Panama slots improved to 34/day — booking confirmed for 22 July.

routeOptions.label: West Africa offshore — standard Cape–Europe track
routeOptions.notes: Track passes 160+ nm off the Niger Delta piracy box; BMP-WA hardening in effect.

disruptions.title: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb security escalation
disruptions.description: Nine corroborated signals over 60 hours: missile and drone attacks on merchant tonnage, SEVERE UKMTO threat level, war-risk premiums ×4, and two major carriers diverting. Container vessels are the preferred target class (71% of incidents).

disruptions.title: Typhoon Mirinae — Luzon Strait / Taiwan corridor
disruptions.description: Category 3 typhoon crossing the main transpacific departure corridor; recurvature vs landfall uncertain for 48 h. Port closures possible in Taiwan from 15 July.

disruptions.title: Singapore–Klang bunker & berth congestion (reroute knock-on)
disruptions.description: Cape diversions concentrated bunker demand (+22%) and re-sequenced port rotations, pushing Port Klang berth waiting to 24–30 h and Singapore barge lead times to 3–4 days.

disruptions.title: Gulf of Guinea kidnap-for-ransom activity
disruptions.description: Third crew kidnapping this quarter, 90 nm off Brass. Risk concentrated within 150 nm of the Niger Delta; Cape–Europe through-traffic advised to hold 150+ nm offshore.

disruptions.title: Panama Canal draft-restriction rumour (contradicted by ACP)
disruptions.description: A single secondary-source report suggested Gatún Lake levels could fall again in August, hinting at returning draft restrictions. The authoritative ACP signal shows the opposite — booking slots raised 31→34/day and draft stable at 49 ft — so the cluster is held at monitoring only.

disruptions.title: Transpacific schedule slack — VYG-2026-0002 ahead of LA berth window
disruptions.description: AIS schedule telemetry flagged MV Jade Horizon running 14 h ahead of the confirmed Los Angeles Pier 400 berth window (20–22 July) — pure schedule waste convertible into fuel and CO₂ savings via slow-steaming. Raised from voyage telemetry and terminal confirmations rather than external news signals.

decisions.title: Reroute VYG-2026-0007 via Cape of Good Hope with slow-steaming

recommendation.headline: Divert MV OceanMind Harmony to Route Option B (Cape of Good Hope), slow-steam the Wild Coast and Dakar segments, and shift top-up bunkering to Straits Marine Energy at Port Klang.
actions: Adopt Route Option B (Cape of Good Hope) before the vessel clears the Malacca Strait — divergence point in ~14 h.
Slow-steam segments Durban→Cape Town and Dakar→Canaries at 16.0 kn (from 19.5 kn), cutting the CO₂ penalty from +11.8% to +5.9%.
Bunker 620 t VLSFO + 180 t B24 biofuel at Port Klang with Straits Marine Energy (SUP-001) — USD 9/t under Singapore spot, ISCC EU chain of custody.
Notify charterer Meridian Container Line of revised ETA Rotterdam 12 Aug (+7.5 days) with evidence pack attached.
Cancel provisional Suez convoy slot request and release war-risk cover quote (saves ≈ USD 400k premium).

decisions.rationale: Nine corroborated signals establish a sustained targeting pattern against large container tonnage in the Bab el-Mandeb corridor. Continuing via Suez prices in a USD ~400k war-risk premium, convoy-slot delay risk (2/week), and unquantifiable crew risk. The Cape routing is 3,400 nm longer, but slow-steaming two segments exploits the cubic speed–fuel relationship to hold the CO₂ penalty to +5.9% and the fuel-cost delta to +USD 182k — a net saving of ≈ USD 218k versus escorted Suez transit once premium and delay-risk are counted. FuelEU GHG-intensity remains compliant (B24 blend at Port Klang improves the balance), and the 2026 EU ETS 70% phase-in adds only USD 18.7k liability on the incremental emissions.

alternatives.label: Continue via Suez with armed escort / convoy slot
alternatives.summary: Hold Route Option A, book coalition convoy (next slot 19 July), accept 0.9% hull-value war-risk premium.
alternatives.rejectionReason: War-risk premium ≈ USD 400k exceeds the reroute cost delta; convoy capacity (12 vessels, 2/week) is oversubscribed 3:1; and this vessel class draws 71% of attacks. Residual crew-safety risk is not compensable.

alternatives.label: Cape of Good Hope at full sea speed (Option C)
alternatives.summary: Divert via the Cape but maintain 19.5 kn throughout to limit the ETA slip to +5.5 days.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Burns +168 t more fuel than the slow-steam plan for only 2 days of schedule recovery; doubles the CO₂ penalty (+11.8% vs +5.9%), doubles the EU ETS charge, and degrades the vessel's CII trajectory from B to C.

alternatives.label: Hold at Singapore anchorage awaiting de-escalation
alternatives.summary: Anchor off Singapore up to 7 days, then transit Suez if the threat level drops.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Previous escalation cycles took 6–14 weeks to normalise (SIG-0009 historical base rates) — a 7-day hold most likely converts into a late Cape diversion anyway, stacking the delay on top of the reroute. Anchorage congestion (SIG-0010) adds cost with no risk reduction.

evidence.label: 9 corroborated security signals in 60 h
evidence.detail: Missile near-miss (SIG-0001), UKMTO SEVERE (SIG-0002), small-arms fire (SIG-0008) — independent sources: Reuters, Lloyd's List, UKMTO, TradeWinds.

evidence.label: Container tonnage is the preferred target class (71% of attacks)
evidence.detail: Ambrey pattern analysis of 31 incidents since May 2026 (SIG-0039) — directly applicable to a 14,000 TEU vessel.

evidence.label: War-risk premium quantified at ≈ USD 400k
evidence.detail: 0.9% of insured hull value (SIG-0003), quadrupled from 0.22% baseline; several syndicates declining container tonnage.

evidence.label: Carbon calc: +11.8% raw → +5.9% with slow-steaming
evidence.detail: carbon.compare(routeA, routeB): VLSFO EF 3.151 tCO₂/t · Suez 2,850 t → 8,980 tCO₂; Cape@19.5kn 3,186 t → 10,040 tCO₂ (+11.8%); Cape w/ 2 slow-steam segments 3,018 t → 9,510 tCO₂ (+5.9%). Speed-cube rule: (16.0/19.5)³ = 0.55× segment consumption.

evidence.label: EU ETS 2026 liability delta: +USD 18.7k
evidence.detail: 530 tCO₂ incremental × 50% extra-EU voyage scope × 70% 2026 phase-in × €72/EUA × 1.08 USD/EUR × 1.297 finance provisioning uplift ≈ USD 18.7k (CH₄/N₂O in scope, negligible on VLSFO).

evidence.label: FuelEU GHG-intensity check: PASS
evidence.detail: Voyage blend incl. 180 t B24 at Port Klang → 87.1 gCO₂e/MJ vs 89.34 limit (−2.5%). ISCC EU chain of custody available from SUP-001.

evidence.label: Supplier DNA: Straits Marine Energy 96/100 reliability, 0 incidents
evidence.detail: 212 deliveries YTD, zero quantity or quality incidents, USD 9/t under Singapore spot amid barge congestion (SIG-0010, SIG-0034).

evidence.label: Cape-route weather within seasonal norms
evidence.detail: Agulhas abnormal-wave advisory (SIG-0016) is a standing winter pattern handled by the slow-steam plan; no tropical systems on the Atlantic leg.

decisions.reliabilityNote: Evidence complete — 8/8 checks passed: signal corroboration ≥3 sources, deterministic cost/carbon calcs reproduced twice, no conflicting signals, all regulatory citations current.

decisions.title: Shift VYG-2026-0003 bunkering from spot barge to Meridian Bunkering window

recommendation.headline: Lock a confirmed Meridian Bunkering Singapore barge window for 16 July instead of waiting spot, avoiding a 3–4 day barge queue.
actions: Book Meridian Bunkering (SUP-002) barge slot 16 July 04:00–10:00 SGT.
Take 240 t VLSFO (vs 405 t plan) — sufficient to Qingdao with 18% reserve; defer balance to cheaper CFR Qingdao market.
Hold transit speed; no route change required.

decisions.rationale: Singapore barge lead times blew out to 3–4 days on reroute-driven demand (+22% w/w). A confirmed window with a 92-reliability supplier avoids a likely 2-day idle at anchorage (≈ USD 34k TCE loss) for a modest USD 4/t premium.

alternatives.label: Wait for spot barge availability
alternatives.summary: Stay in the spot queue; savings USD 4/t if a slot appears in time.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Expected 2-day anchorage idle costs ~USD 34k against a USD 1k fuel saving.

evidence.label: MPA barge congestion signal
evidence.detail: Bunker sales +22% w/w; VLSFO barge slots quoted 3–4 days (SIG-0010).

evidence.label: Supplier DNA: Meridian 92/100 reliability
evidence.detail: 486 deliveries YTD, one low-severity scheduling slip in March.

decisions.reliabilityNote: Evidence complete — cost model reproduced, supplier record verified.

approval.comment: Confirmed window booked. Good catch on the queue risk.

decisions.title: Southern deviation for VYG-2026-0005 around Typhoon Mirinae

recommendation.headline: Adopt the southern deviation (Route B) keeping 240+ nm from Typhoon Mirinae's forecast track; accept +1.5 days ETA.
actions: Divert to Route B immediately — southern track via 21°N before turning northeast.
Re-evaluate at 06:00Z daily against JTWC forecast updates; recurvature could allow an earlier northward cut.
Advise Long Beach terminal of revised ETA 27 July.

decisions.rationale: The original great-circle track crosses Mirinae's 72 h forecast cone. Heavy-weather transit risks container loss and structural stress on a 10,000 TEU vessel with high deck stacks. The southern deviation adds 310 nm (+85 t fuel) but keeps separation above the 200 nm company minimum. Forecast confidence is moderate (cone still wide), hence REVIEW rather than READY.

alternatives.label: Hold original great-circle track
alternatives.summary: Maintain Route A and rely on the typhoon recurving northeast before intercept.
alternatives.rejectionReason: 40% of JTWC ensemble members keep Mirinae on an intercepting track — unacceptable parametric-roll exposure.

alternatives.label: Delay departure-adjacent waypoint by 36 h
alternatives.summary: Slow to 12 kn for 36 h and let the system pass ahead.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Leaves the vessel in the trailing swell field and forfeits schedule with similar net delay to the deviation.

evidence.label: JTWC Category 3 advisory
evidence.detail: 100 kt sustained, WNW at 12 kt; 72 h cone spans the planned track (SIG-0014).

evidence.label: Voyage calc: deviation cost model
evidence.detail: +310 nm at 19 kn → +36 h, +85 t VLSFO, +268 tCO₂ (voyage_calc.deviation).

decisions.reliabilityNote: Human review advised — forecast-cone uncertainty exceeds threshold (ensemble spread 420 nm at 72 h). Recommendation is safe-side; review daily.

decisions.title: Slow-steam VYG-2026-0002 transpacific leg for FuelEU pool credit

recommendation.headline: Reduce transpacific speed 18.5 → 17.0 kn, arriving inside the LA berth window while banking 96 tCO₂e toward the fleet FuelEU pool.
actions: Set 17.0 kn from 155°E; berth window at Los Angeles (20–22 July) still met with 8 h buffer.
Credit the 96 tCO₂e saving to the fleet FuelEU compliance pool.

decisions.rationale: The vessel was running 14 h ahead of its berth window — pure schedule waste. The speed-cube rule converts that slack into a 3.9% fuel saving on the remaining leg with zero commercial impact.

alternatives.label: Maintain 18.5 kn and anchor off San Pedro
alternatives.summary: Arrive early and wait at anchorage.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Burns 30 t more fuel to wait at anchor — strictly dominated by slow-steaming.

evidence.label: Berth window confirmation
evidence.detail: LA Pier 400 window 20 July 18:00 – 22 July 06:00 PDT confirmed by terminal.

decisions.reliabilityNote: Evidence complete — deterministic saving, no downside identified.

decisions.title: Security posture for VYG-2026-0008 transit past the Gulf of Guinea

recommendation.headline: Escalated to the company security officer: embarked-escort quotes conflict with flag-state guidance on the current transit corridor.
actions: Hold current 160 nm offshore track (already outside the incident concentration box).
Escalate escort decision: private embarked team (USD 46k) vs flag-state advice that offshore track needs none.
Maintain BMP-WA hardening: doubled lookouts, citadel drill completed 13 July, AIS continuous.

decisions.rationale: The kidnapping 90 nm off Brass (SIG-0027) sits 380 nm east of the vessel's track. Historical incidents beyond 150 nm offshore are rare, but the charterer's security policy mandates escort quotes after any regional kidnap event — and the two inputs now conflict. Agent policy: conflicting authoritative guidance → ESCALATE, not recommend.

alternatives.label: Contract embarked security team at Lomé
alternatives.summary: Divert 6 h to embark a 3-man team for the West Africa leg.
alternatives.rejectionReason: Not rejected — held pending security-officer ruling; cost is defensible if policy requires it.

evidence.label: IMB kidnap incident 90 nm off Brass
evidence.detail: Third KFR incident this quarter; concentration within 150 nm of Niger Delta (SIG-0027).

evidence.label: Conflicting guidance detected
evidence.detail: Charterer security policy §4.2 (escort after regional KFR) vs Greek flag-state circular 2026-11 (no escort needed >150 nm offshore).

decisions.reliabilityNote: Conflicting authoritative inputs — charterer policy and flag-state guidance disagree; human security officer must rule. No autonomous recommendation issued.

decisions.title: Panama draft-restriction contingency for VYG-2026-0006

recommendation.headline: No action recommended — a single uncorroborated report of returning draft restrictions does not meet the evidence bar.
actions: Maintain Panama routing and 22 July booking slot.
Watch ACP daily advisories; auto-rerun this pipeline if a restriction is gazetted.

decisions.rationale: One secondary-source report suggested Gatún levels might fall again in August. The authoritative signal (SIG-0017, Panama Canal Authority) shows the opposite: slots raised to 34/day and drafts stable at 49 ft. One low-confidence source contradicted by the primary authority = insufficient evidence to act.

alternatives.label: Pre-emptively rebook via Magellan Strait
alternatives.summary: Avoid Panama entirely on the southbound leg.
alternatives.rejectionReason: +9 days and +USD 385k against a rumour contradicted by the canal authority itself.

evidence.label: ACP primary signal contradicts the rumour
evidence.detail: Slots raised 31→34/day, Gatún recovering, draft unchanged (SIG-0017).

decisions.reliabilityNote: Single uncorroborated secondary report vs authoritative primary source — evidence-completeness gate blocks any action recommendation.

events.title: Signal ingestion sweep complete
events.detail: Ingested 40 signals from the last 96 h across GDELT news, UKMTO advisories, port authorities and market feeds. 12 signals reference the Red Sea corridor — 4× the trailing-30-day baseline for that geography.

events.title: Clustering: 9 signals form one coherent event
events.detail: DBSCAN over (geo, time, entity) space clusters SIG-0001/0002/0003/0004/0005/0006/0008/0009/0039 into a single disruption: kinetic attacks on merchant shipping at Bab el-Mandeb with insurance and carrier-behaviour knock-ons. Cluster silhouette 0.87 — clean separation from background noise.

events.title: Corroboration check: 9 independent sources
events.detail: Cross-source verification: Reuters, Lloyd's List, UKMTO, TradeWinds, Suez Canal Authority, Bloomberg, Ambrey. No single-source claims in the cluster core. Corroboration score 0.97 — well above the 0.6 action threshold.

events.title: Severity escalated to CRITICAL
events.detail: Escalation drivers: (1) kinetic attacks on merchant tonnage, (2) war-risk premium ×4 in 48 h, (3) two top-5 carriers already diverting, (4) targeting pattern skewed to large container vessels — 71% of incidents vs 38% of transits.

events.title: Fleet exposure scan: 2 voyages intersect the threat corridor
events.detail: Route-intersection query over 8 active voyages: VYG-2026-0007 (Suez plan of record, Bab el-Mandeb transit in ~9 days — 14,000 TEU container, the highest-risk target class) and VYG-2026-0004 (VLCC, Hormuz–Malacca routing, no Red Sea transit — monitoring only). VYG-2026-0007 flagged for full pipeline.

events.title: Handoff → Causal Impact Agent
events.detail: Disruption DSR-001 (CRITICAL, corroboration 0.97) with exposure set {VYG-2026-0007} passed to causal analysis. Decision clock started: vessel reaches the route divergence point in ~14 h.

events.title: Building causal graph from disruption cluster
events.detail: Constructing DAG: Bab el-Mandeb escalation → (war-risk repricing, convoy scarcity) → Suez transit risk ↑ → carrier reroute pressure → (Cape traffic ↑, Suez transits −38%) → SE-Asia bunker/berth congestion → VYG-2026-0007 plan-of-record viability degraded.

events.title: First-order impact: Suez plan risk score 82/100
events.detail: Plan-of-record risk decomposition: security 48 (kinetic attack likelihood × target-class multiplier 1.9), insurance 18 (premium ×4, cover withdrawal risk), schedule 16 (convoy slots oversubscribed 3:1). Composite 82 — far above the 40-point action threshold.

events.title: Second-order effects: congestion propagation to Klang/Singapore
events.detail: Reroute wave is already congesting the vessel's own origin region: Port Klang berth waiting 24–30 h (SIG-0011), Singapore barge lead 3–4 days (SIG-0010), VLSFO +5.5% (SIG-0034). Any plan requiring a SE-Asia bunker call must lock supply NOW, before the vessel exits the strait.

events.title: Counterfactual: do-nothing trajectory quantified
events.detail: If no action: vessel reaches Bab el-Mandeb ~23 July under SEVERE threat; war-risk premium ≈ USD 400k (0.9% hull value); convoy wait adds 2–3 days at an exposed anchorage; P(further escalation before transit) estimated 0.35 from historical cycle base rates (6–14 week normalisation).

events.title: Causal graph validated — 9 nodes, 10 edges, no cycles
events.detail: Root cause traced: single origin event (Bab el-Mandeb escalation) explains 100% of the plan-of-record risk delta. Edge confidences 0.72–0.97. Graph published for the decision evidence pack.

events.title: Handoff → Scenario Simulation Agent
events.detail: Causal model + do-nothing counterfactual passed to simulation. Constraint set attached: charterer delivery window Rotterdam ≤ 15 Aug, crew-safety policy (no SEVERE-corridor transit without board sign-off), FuelEU compliance must hold.

events.title: Enumerating feasible action space: 4 scenarios
events.detail: Candidate scenarios: (A) hold Suez plan + convoy escort; (B) Cape of Good Hope + slow-steam 2 segments; (C) Cape at full sea speed; (D) hold at Singapore anchorage 7 days awaiting de-escalation. Infeasible options pruned: air-freight transload (cost ×11), Arctic NSR (no ice-class, insurance void).

events.title: voyage_calc.route(A: Suez baseline)
events.detail: Computing distance/time/fuel for Route A: Port Klang → Rotterdam via Bab el-Mandeb & Suez at 19.5 kn service speed, VLSFO consumption curve for 14,000 TEU class, July monsoon speed-loss factor applied on the Arabian Sea leg.

events.title: Route A: 8,320 nm · 24.0 d · 2,850 t VLSFO · USD 1.653M
events.detail: Baseline confirmed vs plan of record (Δ < 0.5%). Add-ons: war-risk premium ≈ USD 400k (0.9% hull value per SIG-0003), convoy wait 48–72 h at Gulf of Aden anchorage. Fuel priced at Singapore VLSFO USD 580/t contract.

events.title: voyage_calc.route(B/C: Cape of Good Hope)
events.detail: Computing Cape routing: Port Klang → Malacca → SW Indian Ocean → Cape of Good Hope → West Africa offshore (160+ nm) → Rotterdam. Variant B slow-steams Durban→Cape Town and Dakar→Canaries segments at 16.0 kn; variant C holds 19.5 kn throughout.

events.title: Route C (full speed): 11,720 nm · 29.5 d · 3,186 t · +USD 284k
events.detail: Cape at 19.5 kn: +3,400 nm vs Suez, ETA +5.5 d, fuel +336 t (+USD 284k at blended price). No war-risk premium, no convoy dependency. Agulhas winter advisory (SIG-0016) handled by standard offshore routing.

events.title: Route B (slow-steam ×2): 11,720 nm · 31.5 d · 3,018 t · +USD 182k
events.detail: Speed-cube rule on 2 segments: (16.0/19.5)³ = 0.55× consumption over 2,150 nm of segments → saves 168 t vs full-speed Cape. Net vs Suez baseline: ETA +7.5 d, fuel +168 t / +USD 182k (includes SUP-001 price advantage of USD 9/t on the Port Klang stem).

events.title: carbon.compare(baseline=A, candidates=[B, C])
events.detail: IMO CO₂ emission factors: VLSFO 3.151 tCO₂/t fuel (MGO 3.206, HFO 3.114). Computing absolute and percentage deltas for each candidate route, plus EU ETS and FuelEU positions.

events.title: CO₂: A = 8,980 t · C = 10,040 t (+11.8%) · B = 9,510 t (+5.9%)
events.detail: Slow-steaming halves the reroute carbon penalty: Route C raw +11.8% vs baseline; Route B lands at +5.9% (+530 tCO₂). Route B is the carbon-efficient diversion.

events.title: EU ETS 2026: Route B liability delta +USD 18.7k
events.detail: 2026 phase-in = 70% of emissions surrendered (100% from 2027); CH₄ & N₂O in scope from 1 Jan 2026 (negligible on VLSFO). Extra-EU voyage → 50% scope. 530 t × 0.5 × 0.7 × €72 × 1.08 × 1.297 provisioning uplift = USD 18.7k. Route C would cost USD 37.4k.

events.title: FuelEU GHG-intensity: Route B = 87.1 gCO₂e/MJ → PASS
events.detail: With 180 t B24 biofuel blended at Port Klang (ISCC EU certified, SUP-001), voyage GHG intensity = 87.1 gCO₂e/MJ vs the 89.34 limit — 2.5% compliance headroom. Without the bio stem: 90.8 → marginal FAIL. Bunker plan is therefore load-bearing for compliance.

events.title: Scenario D (hold at anchor) simulated and dominated
events.detail: Holding 7 days at Singapore anchorage: +USD 61k (anchorage, idle fuel, crew) with P(still must divert) ≈ 0.65 given 6–14 week historical normalisation cycles. Expected total delay 11.2 days — worse than committing to the Cape now on every axis except optionality.

events.title: Handoff → Decision Agent with 4 fully-costed scenarios
events.detail: Scenario matrix complete: cost, ETA, CO₂, EU ETS, FuelEU, risk score per option. All deterministic numbers reproduced twice (tool double-run) with zero drift. Passing to constraint filtering and ranking.

events.title: Hard constraints filtered the option set
events.detail: Constraint pass: (1) crew-safety policy — no SEVERE-corridor transit without board sign-off → Scenario A requires escalation beyond ops authority; (2) charterer window Rotterdam ≤ 15 Aug → B (12 Aug) and C (10 Aug) both pass; (3) FuelEU compliance → all pass WITH the B24 stem. Surviving: B, C, D.

events.title: Carbon-aware ranking: B > C > D
events.detail: Objective = total economic cost + carbon shadow price (€72/t full emissions, not just ETS scope) + risk penalty. B: +182k fuel + 18.7k ETS + 38k carbon-shadow − 400k premium avoided = net −161k vs do-nothing, risk 28. C: net −77k, risk 30, CII rating degrades B→C. D: net +61k, risk 58. Route B dominates.

events.title: Bunker plan optimised: Straits Marine Energy, Port Klang
events.detail: Cape routing needs +168 t and the B24 stem before departure from the region. Supplier DNA ranking at reachable ports: SUP-001 Straits Marine (rel 96, ESG 91, B24 ISCC, USD 9/t under Singapore spot, zero incidents) beats SUP-002 Meridian (barge queue 3–4 d) and Durban top-up (USD +28/t, 4–6 d lead, SIG-0033).

events.title: RECOMMENDATION: Route B + slow-steam ×2 + SUP-001 bunker shift
events.detail: Divert via Cape of Good Hope with two slow-steam segments; bunker 620 t VLSFO + 180 t B24 at Port Klang with Straits Marine Energy. Impact: ETA +7.5 d, fuel +USD 182k, CO₂ +5.9% (halved from +11.8% raw), EU ETS +USD 18.7k, avoids ≈ USD 400k war-risk premium and all convoy exposure. FuelEU: PASS with 2.5% headroom.

events.title: Reliability gate: READY — evidence complete
events.detail: Evidence-completeness checklist 8/8: ≥3 independent sources per load-bearing claim ✓; deterministic calcs double-run with zero drift ✓; no unresolved conflicting signals ✓; regulatory citations current (EU 2023/957, EU 2023/1805) ✓; supplier verification current ✓; counterfactual quantified ✓; alternatives documented with rejection reasons ✓; decision reversible until Malacca exit (−14 h) ✓.
